hints.TestBucket: Use x >= 0 && x <= 100 style conditions in an if / else if chain, or a tagless switch.
hints.TestDescribePair: Check the cases in the given order: the first one that matches wins. 'y is not 5' is y != 5.
hints.TestOdds: Loop i from 0 to n inclusive; if i%2 == 0 { continue }; otherwise append i.
hints.TestFirstMultiple: for i := start; ; i++ { if i%k == 0 { return i } } (or break out of the loop and return after it).
hints.TestGrid: Two nested for loops; append fmt.Sprintf("%d,%d", i, j).
hints.TestIndexValues: for i, v := range xi { ... fmt.Sprintf("%d:%d", i, v) }
hints.TestAgeOf: if age, ok := m[name]; ok { ... } else { ... }

quiz.q: What does fmt.Println(true && false || true) print?
quiz.why: && binds tighter than ||: (true && false) || true is true.

quiz.q: Does a Go switch case fall through to the next case by default?
options: no, you need the fallthrough keyword
quiz.why: Go cases break automatically. fallthrough opts in.

quiz.q: Which loop keywords does Go have?
quiz.why: for covers classic, while-style, infinite and range loops.

quiz.q: What is the benefit of `if x := f(); x > 3 { }`?
options: x is scoped to the if/else, keeping scope narrow
it allows x to be reassigned
quiz.why: The init statement limits x's scope to the if/else blocks.
